opportunity.title: Scalable GEOINT Architecture IT Contractor Manpower Equivalent (CME) Support
opportunity.description: Request for Proposal W50NH9-27-R-A006 for Scalable Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Architecture IT Contractor Manpower Equivalent support for U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM). Proposals due Nov 13, 2026 with a proposal validity of at least 240 days. Period of performance: one 30-day transition-in, a 12-month base, four 12-month options and one six-month option. Estimated award date Jan 11, 2027. Primarily time and materials, evaluated on a best value trade-off basis.

profile._note: FICTIONAL SAMPLE COMPANY for scenario testing. Not a real firm. Past performance and staffing are invented; only the NAICS codes, set-aside definitions and every opportunity and award figure used against it are real public data.

profile.pastPerformance: HUBZone-certified in rural Oregon. One VA medical-center scheduling tool (about $400K), one county health records integration ($300K).
profile.capacityNotes: Nine staff, all in the HUBZone. No clearance. Small, focused on clinical scheduling software.
verification: NAICS codes confirmed against USAspending reference (api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/references/naics) on 2026-10-16.
Set-asides follow SBA definitions: SBA = small business, 8A = 8(a) Business Development, HUBZONE, WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB.

checks.reason: Full and open competition; no set-aside required.
NAICS 541519 is in the company's codes.
Place of performance is not stated in the notice; verify before bidding.

rationale.point: The solicitation is full and open (no set-aside) for scalable GEOINT architecture IT contractor manpower equivalent support for U.S. Army INSCOM, indicating a large-scale, complex requirement likely demanding significant staffing, clearances, and specialized GEOINT experience.

Cascade HUBZone Software Co. has only 9 staff, no clearances, and past performance limited to clinical scheduling software ($400K VA) and health records integration ($300K county), which does not align with GEOINT architecture or DoD manpower-equivalent support.
The median of top awards for DoD NAICS 541519 is $151.9M, far exceeding the company's capacity and past contract values, making competitive bidding unrealistic.

risks: Inability to meet staffing, clearance, or technical requirements for GEOINT architecture support
Extremely low probability of award against large, experienced competitors in a full-and-open competition
Significant proposal preparation cost with near-zero return on investment
Potential reputational harm from non-responsive or non-compliant submission
nextSteps: Target HUBZone set-aside opportunities aligned with clinical scheduling and health IT expertise
Explore teaming arrangements as a niche subcontractor on larger DoD contracts if clearance and staffing gaps can be mitigated
Invest in facility clearance sponsorship and staff growth if pursuing DoD work long-term
Monitor USAspending for small-business set-aside awards in NAICS 541519 with relevant scope
